problems.title: Almost-everywhere kernel data do not control atomic energies
problems.source_location: PDF pp3-5: Eq1.12, H1-H3, Theorem1.4(ii)(a), Theorem1.6/Eq1.19; definitions p8
problems.assumptions: d=1,s=-1,rho=delta0. W=K except W(0)=0; K=2pi²(x²-x+1/6) periodic. H1 holds by downward semicontinuous modification; H2 and quantitative lower bound c=1 hold because W_hat(k)=k^-2. H3 holds with C1=1+pi²/6,C=1+pi²/2, since 1<=C1+W<=C.
problems.check: Integral energy at delta0 is0, spectral expression pi²/6, distance to uniform1/2. For nu=(delta0+delta1/2)/2 energy=-pi²/24<0. Independently Wtilde=K except Wtilde(0)=-pi² has essential-sup difference0 and delta0 attains the global lower energy bound -pi²/2.
problems.result: Counterexamples to the stated all-probability-measure energy theorem and essential-sup perturbation theorem, plus uniform-minimizer assertion.
problems.counterevidence: Full text contains no density restriction or canonical pointwise convention for general W. Pointwise-sup reading fixes only the perturbation step. Theorem1.1/canonical Riesz kernels not refuted.
problems.impact: Core energy applications; Major in reviewed v1. No finding assigned to unavailable journal-final text.
problems.correction: Restricted L2-density repair via Young and Parseval proved in report. Pointwise bounded perturbation repair verified conditional on valid base all-measure energy bound. Full arbitrary singular-kernel repair not asserted.

problems.title: Missing logarithm in the beta=1 radial integral
problems.check: The displayed annular integral equals |S^(d-1)| integral_(1/R)^1 r^(beta-2)dr = |S^(d-1)| log R at beta1, whereas the proposed bound is2C.
problems.result: Uniform scalar-integral bound false; no counterexample to Lemma3.6.
problems.counterevidence: Sharper oscillatory decay may be true, but does not validate the written intermediate inequality.
problems.impact: Local proof estimate; same multiplier scaling restored.
problems.correction: Keep R^(-d-1)(1+log R), which is L1. Periodization gives L1 bound; Schwartz Fourier sum gives Linfinity; interpolate.

independent_acceptance_scope.result: Both existing problems are confirmed. P1 supplies all-hypothesis counterexamples to the printed arbitrary-probability-measure energy and perturbation conclusions. P2 identifies a genuinely false intermediate scalar inequality while preserving the needed multiplier estimate by a logarithmic endpoint bound.
counterevidence_and_severity_basis: P1 is Major because the hypotheses H1?H3 do permit downward changes at a point, and the asserted energy theorem samples that value for atoms; it directly defeats a quantified main application, not just an unproved proof step. The principal Riesz-potential distance theorem is not refuted.

P2 is Minor because retaining the logarithm leaves an integrable tail and the exact downstream scaling follows from periodization, the direct Schwartz Fourier bound and interpolation. No counterexample to Lemma3.6 is asserted.
